messages:
Alex M.: Heads up — want to run a full KMS rotation simulation next Tue (canary + staged rewrap) to validate envelope compatibility, RBAC changes, and audit logs. Thoughts?
Maria C.: +1. Prefer morning window. want to include both AWS KMS + GCP KMS flows?
Zane P.: yes include both. also test Azure Key Vault path (we haven't exercised it since last infra change).
Kim J.: for the simulation we should clearly define fallback behaviour: if rewrap fails for blobstore objects, services must 1) fall back to old kek variant, 2) queue retry with exponential backoff, and 3) emit a security.audit event.
Alex M.: agreed. can we codify the fallback as part of the canary policy? e.g., canary nodes attempt rewrap, if >5% fail then abort rollout and open incident.
Maria C.: sounds right. what about header versioning? we need to ensure older clients tolerate new envelope headers.
Zane P.: we added a versioned header field last quarter: `enc_ver`. plan: canary writes new `enc_ver:2`, older readers should fallback to previous parsing. document is here: https://redwood.internal/docs/encryption#envelope-versions
Kim J.: testing checklist:
- rotate KEK in KMS (auto rotate path + manual rewrap run)
- run canary against small keyspace (5k objects)
- validate DB rows with encrypted payloads (pg)
- verify cache invalidation and rolling restarts don't drop requests
- RBAC: grant temporary `rewrap-operator` role and audit all GRANTs
sec-oncall: adding incident criteria:
- SEV if rewrap failures >5% for 10m or if audit events stop being emitted
- Pager triggers if auth errors spike >3x baseline
Alex M.: ops-bot — create a temporary role with least privilege for the run and attach 1-hour TTL.
ops-bot: created role `rekey-runner-2024-11-07` with TTL 1h, policy attached, audit trail enabled (role id: rrr-85f2).
Maria C.: good. also need to ensure KMS policy bindings are logged. AWS CloudTrail and GCP Audit logs must be retained for 30d for the drill.
Zane P.: will add stackdriver export and run a test log write: `gcloud logging write test-rotation \"rotation test\" --payload-type json`
Kim J.: include a vuln triage step: if any service indicates use of legacy crypto (non-AEAD), we must pause and open a security review.
Alex M.: what about automatic rotation vs manual rewrap? plan is: rotate KEK automatically in KMS, but perform manual rewrap job (controlled rollout) for data plane. we don't want automatic transparent rewrap without validation.
Maria C.: agree — automatic KEK rotation in KMS is fine (it just updates DEKs), but rewrap must be an explicit job we control. add canary + staged percentages: 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100% with 30m observation windows.
Zane P.: add metric checks for quality/regression: latency p95, error rate, and checksum match rate for rewrapped objects.
Kim J.: add an integrity test: after rewrap, compute HMAC over plaintext-derived metadata and compare with pre-wrap expected value. include sample script in runbook:```bash
# fetch obj, decrypt with old DEK, encrypt with new DEK
python tools/rewrap.py --object-id $OBJ --old-kek sk_old --new-kek sk_new --dry-run
```
sec-oncall: also ensure alerting for audit log gaps: if we don't see `security.audit.rewrap` events for >10m during rollout, auto-pause.
Alex M.: timeline? propose Wed 09:00 UTC for canary start, 2h low-traffic window. final roll next Friday if canary passes.
Maria C.: can we also pre-run a dry-run that only writes logs and doesn't mutate DB/binaries? schedule Thu 09:00 for dry-run. that way we validate pipelines.
Zane P.: will prepare test fixtures — 10k small objects + 200 medium blobs + 50 large blobs. will coordinate S3 bucket and GCS prefix.
Kim J.: RBAC checklist:
- ensure `rekey-runner-*` roles cannot perform `kms:CreateKey` or escalate privileges
- run `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` against role to confirm no extra perms
- snapshot IAM bindings before and after
Maria C.: audit retention note: extend retention to 90d for the trial logs in a restricted bucket for postmortem.
Alex M.: vuln triage: if we find any object encrypted with unsupported algorithm, abort and switch to incident flow. who's owner of the incident doc? sec-oncall you maintain it right?
sec-oncall: I own the incident playbook. I'll spawn a channel `#inc-rot-2024-11-07` when run begins. include runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-rotation-drill
ops-bot: canary rollout policy created: percentages [1,5,20,50,100], pause_on_signal: true, max_fail_percent: 5.
Maria C.: any special customer data considerations? for regulated tenants we should run rewrap in their private VPC and coordinate support.
Alex M.: note: for Dedicated customers with HSM-backed keys, we'll coordinate with their contacts; schedule will be out-of-band.
Zane P.: I'll open a short RFC doc with detailed steps and include rollback commands. rough rollback: rewrap-runner --rollback-to kek_id=old_kek --time-window 30m
Kim J.: final preflight checklist before canary:
- smoke test decrypt/encrypt on staging 
- RBAC role created and validated
- audit export configured and retention set
- runbook and incident channel created
- metric dashboards live (p95, error rate, rewrap success %)
Alex M.: perfect. I'll send calendar invites and mark owners on each checklist item. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Maria C.: thanks — I'll coordinate with Compliance on retention notes.
Zane P.: will push tools/rewrap.py update to main and tag for the drill.
sec-oncall: standing by for the channel creation and watch rotations. good plan.
